transformations.title: Translation: Every Point Moves the Same Way

inputs.text: A translation slides a figure@1 without changing anything else: every point moves the same distance in the same direction@2. Shape, size and orientation are all kept, and the image is named vertex for vertex@3 — A prime, B prime, C prime.
A rotation turns the figure@1 around a point — here a quarter turn@2. Lengths and angles survive the turn; what changes is the way the figure faces, and the names turn with it@3.
A reflection flips the figure@1 like a mirror@2. Lengths and angles are still the same, but the vertices are read in the opposite order@3.

order-of-operations.title: The Order Operations Are Done In

inputs.text: Operations are not done left to right. Brackets first, then the multiplications and divisions, and only then the additions and subtractions. So in this expression@1 the division and the product collapse first@2, each on its own, and the plus and the minus wait their turn.

Brackets say: this is one number, work it out before anything else touches it. So here@1 the inside goes first@2, and only then the multiplication. Without the brackets the product would come first and the answer would not be the same.
